text:
Maya: heads-up — noticed the p95 on the service overview dropped ~120ms this morning but per-endpoint p95s didn't move. looks like a rollup mismatch 🤔
jon: can you paste the dashboard query? might be an aggregation mismatch (route vs path) or tag missing during rollout.
Maya: sure — the top panel uses this promql: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))` but the rollup uses `by (le)` only, so routes are getting mixed.
tessa: ah mixing route tags will change distribution shape. the rollup is doing a multi-namespace sum then quantile; that's unsafe unless buckets line up and you keep route cardinality.
jon: we intentionally roll up by service for the overview to reduce cardinality. tradeoff: latency percentiles become dominated by hot routes. maybe p95 at rollup should be computed from per-route p95s with weighted logic, not from histograms merged across routes.
Maya: is there a known bug where histogram_quantile(after-sum) underestimates p99 when one route has many short requests? seen that behavior.
gary: we've hit that before — upstream t-digest vs Prom histograms confusion. For histogram_quantile you must sum buckets (which we do) but if bucket boundaries differ per exporter, results are wrong. do we have routes with custom buckets?
elena: some older services export a 0.1-1s bucket set while newer ones export 0.001-10s. that mismatch will definitely skew rollups.
infra-bot: deploy job queued — PR #2438 (instrumentation: standardize histogram buckets) by gary — scheduled canary at 03:00 UTC :rocket:
jon: immediate short fix: change the overview panel to show percentile of the p95 series computed at route level: `sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) by (route)` then apply quantile over the resulting p95s in the client. downside: more client-side work and more series to fetch.
tessa: alternative: emit summary metrics (like 50/95/99 gauges) at service ingest so rollups are stable. that reduces cardinality but increases cardinality of metrics (one gauge per route).
Maya: I'm leaning toward instrumentation change + a quick UI patch to call out "rollup percentile is approximate" with a tooltip linking to docs. Can someone sketch the small UI change?
elena: I can add a subtle warning (khaki badge) and a link to /docs/telemetry/percentiles. quick PR tonight.
gary: I'll standardize buckets in a PR + add unit tests to check merging behavior. patch will add a `histogram_buckets_version` tag so we can detect mismatches in the telemetry pipeline.
jon: also add a small analyzer job to run nightly that samples routes with contradictory bucket versions and posts to #incidents if >5% traffic affected.
Maya: can we get a reproducible test? I can craft a small prometheus-like check: two fake exporters, one with narrow buckets, one wide, generate traffic 90% small, 10% large, and assert that rollup p95 < expected. I'll add it to infra/telemetry/tests.
tessa: sounds good. next steps: gary PR for buckets (owner), elena UI patch (owner), jon add nightly analyzer, Maya adds repro test. we should schedule a canary for the metrics change before force rolling.
Maya: thanks everyone. marking this thread for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
